content:
I haven't reviewed your contribution in detail yet. A quick review first:

Statement
* The formatting of the league explanation is off. Please refer to the statement of Pentago as an example of how it should look like: https://www.codingame.com/contribute/view/1516179aa763a6302dbdfa2c8676688ed085c3

* Please leave a blank line before every subheading.

* Please avoid creating a wall of text. Break the content down into paragraphs and/or bullet-point lists where appropriate.

* Please add a Victory Conditions section and a Defeat Conditions section. Again, you can refer to Pentago for an example.

Input
* For every input variable, please include its variable type and description.

* There are too many input variables. The contribution guidelines state that the best practice is not to exceed 10 per loop: https://www.codingame.com/playgrounds/40701/help-center/creating-your-own-puzzle

Output
* Please change the heading to "Output each turn".

Input / Constraints
* I don't think leagueLevel and maxTurns are normally provided as inputs.

* maxTurns may remain in the constraints, but leagueLevel should probably be removed.

Thanks.

⚠️ This contribution is currently a work in progress. The core gameplay is complete, but I am still validating game balance, onboarding, league progression and Boss difficulty. Feedback is very welcome!

Hello!

I am submitting ASCII Tycoon, a simultaneous two-player Bot Programming game where each bot manages three business zones while competing on a shared market.

The game includes three progressive leagues, structured bot inputs, grouped purchases (x1, x10 and x100), local and global boosts, visible and secret trophies, and increasingly challenging league Bosses.

The ASCII terminal theme is purely visual: beginners do not need to parse the viewer to create their first bot. English and French statements, automated tests, real-engine Boss tests and a TournamentRunner are included.

I would especially appreciate feedback about game balance, onboarding clarity and the overall player experience.

Thank you for reviewing the contribution!

Thank you for the quick review and for the clear feedback.

I have addressed the requested changes: the league explanation has been reformatted, the statement has been split into clearer paragraphs and lists, blank lines were added before subheadings, and Victory Conditions / Defeat Conditions sections were added.

I also updated the input documentation so every variable has a type and description, simplified the per-turn input protocol, changed the output heading to “Output each turn”, and removed leagueLevel / maxTurns from the bot inputs. maxTurns now only remains as a documented league duration/constraint.

Thanks again for taking the time to review it!

Thank you for the update. The number of variables looks more reasonable now, and the statement also looks much prettier.

However, the following sections still have some formatting issues:

* League introduction section (before "The Goal") should have a green background, with its icon positioned at the top.

* Victory Conditions section should have a teal background, with a trophy icon on the left.

* Defeat Conditions section should have a red background, with a skull icon on the left.

You could examine the HTML source code used by Pentago and apply the same approach to your statement.

I'll try to perform a more detailed review in the coming days.

Thanks again.

I've performed a slightly more detailed review. The following points are in addition to the formatting issues mentioned last time.

The Goal
* Please remove "Your score is totalEarned." The scoring mechanism doesn't belong to this section.

Leagues
* Community-created games can't assign custom names to leagues. You're limited to the standard "Wood League" name, although you're free to decide the number of sub-leagues.

• So, please avoid referring to Wood, Bronze or Legend Leagues. Instead, use neutral references such as "this league", "the next league" and "higher leagues".

Wood League, and the Rule subsections in general
* This section jumps straight into concepts such as available actions, and "locked" items without first explaining what these concepts represent. As a result, a player encountering the game for the first time has to infer too much from the rules.

* Please add some introductory context before listing the available actions, and reconsider the ordering of the subsections, e.g.

  • What the business consists of
  • How income and collecting work
  • How producers and upgrades work
  • What can be purchased in the current league
  • How prices and purchases work
  • How a turn proceeds

* The exact structure is up to you, but the player should understand the basic gameplay before encountering the more technical details. 

League Detection
* Please remove the entire section. The input format being identical across leagues is standard for almost all bot games. Players shouldn't be expected to detect the current league based on inputs.

* Instead, you could add a "What is in store" section, similar to the final part of the Pentago statement. This would be a good place to briefly explain what becomes available in the higher leagues.

Quantities and Gains
* Please state only the parameters that are relevant to the current league. Don't introduce information that the player doesn't yet need.

Input for one game turn

* Please remove "The game loop starts directly with these four lines every turn." This section can go directly into the description of the input lines.

* Please change "(8): turn:int … couponCount:int" to "8 space-separated variables:".

* Similarly, please change the beginning of the next part to "9 space-separated variables:".

* Please change all instances of "int" to "Integer".

* Please format all fixed values using the <const> tag. This includes values such as NONE, OK, 0, 1, ARCADE and -1. Make sure commas aren't included inside the <const> tag.

Final section
* Instead of repeating the goal ("Build the most profitable terminal-themed business"), you could include here:

  • Appropriate credit, if the game is inspired by an existing game.

  • A link to the referee code. This is optional, but providing the referee source is common practice for bot games here.

Before I can perform a genuinely in-depth review of the contribution, I need a clearer statement as described above. Thank you for your understanding.
